info.title: NoResponse API
info.description: NoResponse is an identity and people risk engine. Retain workspace people, investigate their identifiers, read complete source evidence and preserve investigation history. People-read access includes evidence by default; explicit evidence restrictions retain submitted details, job status and coverage. Keep the API key on your server.

post.summary: Rotate the API key that signs the request.
post.description: Mints a new key with the same scopes as the key that signs the request and returns it once. The presented key keeps working for overlap_seconds (default 24 hours, from 60 seconds to 7 days), then answers 401. A key accepts one rotation: rotating again with a key already in its overlap answers 409 key_rotation_in_progress, so rotate with the new key. Rotation is not idempotent: a retry after a lost answer mints another key.

get.description: Lists your webhook endpoints in every state, ordered by endpoint_id, with the ids of their signing keys and without secrets. Requires the webhooks scope.

post.description: Registers a webhook endpoint and returns it with its first signing secret, shown only in this answer: store it where your receiver reads it. The URL is https on port 443 or 8443 with a DNS host whose every address is public; it is checked now and on every delivery. The endpoint starts unverified and receives assessment events once it echoes an endpoint.verification challenge, which sendTestEvent sends. You can hold 5 endpoints. Requires the webhooks scope, and response_mode detailed also the detailed scope. Registration is not idempotent: a retry after a lost answer registers a second endpoint, which you can list and delete.

delete.description: Deletes the endpoint and its signing keys. Deliveries still queued for it are dropped. Requires the webhooks scope. An endpoint that is already gone answers 404.

post.description: Issues a new signing key for the endpoint and returns its secret once. Every delivery from now on is signed with it; the key it replaces keeps verifying for 7 days, so your receiver can hold both while it switches. Requires the webhooks scope. Rotation is not idempotent: a retry after a lost answer issues another key, which replaces the first.

post.summary: Send a test event to an endpoint.
post.description: endpoint.verification sends a signed challenge now and answers whether the endpoint echoed it within 5 seconds; an echo verifies the endpoint, including a disabled one. investigation.completed queues one signed event with test: true and a fixed example investigation, delivered and retried like any other event; the endpoint must be verified. Both use the endpoint's current signing key. Requires the webhooks scope.

get.description: Read the workspace directory with a live key carrying members or members_manage. Member identities and grants belong to this workspace. Owner-controlled issuance limits team automation to authorised service credentials.

patch.description: Update a non-owner member role, environment access or sensitive permission exclusions with a live members_manage key. Owner changes, identity binding and support access remain outside this scope. The current delegation ceiling is checked within the change transaction.

delete.description: Remove a non-owner member with a live members_manage key. Subsequent access is refused and personal credentials are revoked. Independently owned service credentials follow their own lifecycle.

get.description: Read audit events within your current environment permissions. Filters apply before pagination.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Events per page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: next_cursor from the previous page, unchanged; keep every filter unchanged.

parameters.name: environment
parameters.description: Affected scope. API keys can request only their own environment. Omit to read the scopes the caller is allowed.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Exact action, such as key.created or webhook_endpoint.deleted.

parameters.name: actor
parameters.description: Exact external user id, public API key id or console credential id.

parameters.name: target_type
parameters.description: Exact target kind, such as key, member, setting or workspace.

parameters.name: target_id
parameters.description: Public target identifier. Audit targets exclude subject identifiers.

parameters.name: outcome
parameters.description: Exact outcome.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Inclusive creation timestamp in RFC3339 format.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Exclusive creation timestamp in RFC3339 format; must follow since when both are supplied.

get.description: Read daily usage units, screenings included, for the environments you can access. These counts are unpriced. With live access it also returns the daily console lookup cap: used, limit and resets_at.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The first UTC day, as YYYY-MM-DD.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The last UTC day, included, as YYYY-MM-DD; no later than today.

post.description: Create a workspace-bound invite for a non-owner role with a live members_manage key. The new token is returned once. Set external_user_id to bind acceptance to an exact verified provider subject; email is contact information. Creating a token does not send an email.

get.description: Read pending workspace invitations with a live members_manage key. Tokens are excluded. Expiry and token reissue timestamps describe invitation state; they do not establish email delivery.

delete.description: Revoke a pending invitation with a live members_manage key. A revoked token cannot be accepted. Owner-role invitations remain outside machine delegation.

post.description: Create an API key in the signing key environment with authority no greater than the issuer holds. Requires management. Optional name, purpose, kind and expiry describe its lifecycle. Send request_id for safe issuance retries: the first successful response returns the secret once; a repeat returns existing metadata without the secret, and changed parameters conflict. Without request_id a retry can create another key. A service credential is independent of its issuer; personal credentials require an authenticated member and retire when that member loses authority.

get.description: Lists the keys of the signing key's environment, newest first, at most 200, revoked and expired keys included, without secrets: each key's id, prefix, scopes, status, and who created and revoked it. Requires the management scope. Read-only and safe to retry.

delete.description: Revokes a key of the signing key's environment at once: its next request answers 401. Requires the management scope. A key of the other environment or of another workspace answers 404 not_found. A key cannot revoke itself (409 self_revocation): rotate it with keys.rotate, or revoke it with another management key. Revoking a revoked key changes nothing and answers the key as it was revoked, so a retry is safe.

patch.description: Replaces the explicit restrictions on an active key. Restrictions take effect on its next request and survive rotation. The issuer must be able to grant the resulting access in the key environment. A restricted caller cannot remove its own restrictions or grant unrestricted access to another key. Changes are audited without recording the secret.

get.description: Read this environment retention, source selection, daily screening cap and effective flow policies. A flow without its own thresholds inherits account_creation. Requires settings or management. Another environment answers404. Read-only and safe to retry.

patch.description: Change named retention, screening cap, source or flow settings in one transaction. Requires settings or management; changes to active policy also require policy_publish, which legacy management includes. Use expected_policy_version to reject concurrent changes and record a change_reason. Each accepted change creates a fresh version and an atomic audit event. Retention and screening cap edits do not require policy publication authority. Flow thresholds preserve their declared ordering and bounds.

get.description: Every POST the endpoint received, newest first: the event id and type, which attempt it was, whether it was a replay, delivered or failed, the response code, why it failed and how long it took. Attempts are kept for 30 days, or your retention_days when that is shorter, and are deleted with the assessment they carried. Requires the webhooks scope. Read-only and safe to retry. The cursor is opaque and bound to your workspace and the endpoint; a tampered or expired cursor answers 400 invalid_cursor.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Attempts per page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: next_cursor from the previous page, unchanged.

post.description: Queues the event for the endpoint again: the same event id and body it received, with a new NR-Webhook-Timestamp and a signature from the endpoint's current signing key, retried like any other delivery and listed with replay: true. Your receiver deduplicates on the event id. The endpoint must be verified. Requires the webhooks scope. Not idempotent: each call, a retry included, sends the event again.

get.description: Search authenticated request attempts by time, route, status or request correlation id. The interval is at most seven days. Each attempt has a unique id and may include the exact served decision. Records are bounded best effort and exclude request bodies, secrets and source payloads. A repeated correlation id does not overwrite another attempt.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive start of a range of at most seven days.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Exclusive end of the range.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: Optional filter or paging parameter.

parameters.name: route
parameters.description: Optional filter or paging parameter.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Optional filter or paging parameter.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Optional filter or paging parameter.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Optional filter or paging parameter.

parameters.name: api_key_id
parameters.description: Filter by the public authenticated API key identifier; older unattributed rows do not match.

get.description: Read immutable configuration versions in one environment with settings or management. Follow before_version for older records.

post.summary: Restore captured settings as a new guarded version.
post.description: Restore a retained configuration as a fresh version with the expected current version and a change reason. Requires settings plus policy_publish, or legacy management. Restore preserves the historical record and does not undo customer enforcement.

get.description: Read retained erasure progress and downstream acknowledgements. Completion does not certify deletion from backups.

schema.description: Opaque, server-issued erasure receipt id. It contains no subject identifier.

post.description: Count all retained matching request attempts and latency samples within seven days. Capture is best effort.

post.summary: Summarise retained webhook attempts and delivery queue
post.description: Count retained webhook delivery attempts within thirty days and report current retained queue state.

Request an encrypted JSON Lines snapshot of retained account or audit records. Requires exports plus history or audit scope. An account export without legacy history needs investigate with evidence or detailed, because it holds submitted identifiers; detailed account data always needs evidence or detailed. Criteria are frozen and hashed. Each environment permits four active jobs, 64 MiB per artifact, and 256 KiB per chunk. Artifacts expire after 24 hours. Send an Idempotency-Key to safely repeat a request. Every operation checks current permissions and source retention.

get.description: List authorised jobs for one kind and environment. Detailed jobs require current detailed-data permission and are filtered before pagination. Keep the kind and environment unchanged when following next_cursor.

Read the status of an authorised export. Records and bytes describe committed progress in the current generation. Only completed, unexpired artifacts can be downloaded. Source erasure, retention changes and workspace removal can invalidate a job.

post.summary: Cancel and remove an export artifact.
post.description: Cancel an export and remove its stored chunks. Repeating cancellation is safe. An already admitted download may finish; bytes already returned cannot be recalled. Send an empty JSON object.

Start a new generation of a failed export before its original expiry, up to ten generations. The request criteria stay fixed and the new generation takes a fresh source snapshot. Cancelled, erased and expired jobs cannot be retried. Send an empty JSON object.

get.description: Download one chunk of a completed, unexpired export after a fresh permission and privacy check. The response contains base64-encoded JSON Lines, a SHA-256, generation and next index. Decode and concatenate chunks in order from one generation. Audit storage failure withholds the bytes.

get.summary: Read audit retention and available history.
get.description: Read audit retention for the environment. The default is 365 days. Oldest available is an observation; it does not establish uninterrupted capture. Workspace-wide events follow the live storage policy.

patch.description: Set test-environment audit retention from 1 to 365 days with audit_manage scope. Live retention also governs workspace-wide audit events and requires a dashboard member authorised in both environments. Shortening immediately hides older events and invalidates audit exports; extending cannot restore deleted events. External receivers control copies already delivered.

get.description: List audit subscriptions and their endpoint state and latest delivery attempt. Streams use verified HTTPS webhook endpoints and signed audit.event bodies. Delivery is at least once and unordered; deduplicate by webhook id. An empty action filter accepts all actions within the chosen scope.

post.description: Configure the action filter for one verified webhook endpoint. Requires audit_manage. Capture starts at subscription creation; use an audit export for available earlier events. Workspace-wide scope requires an unrestricted console member and is unavailable to API keys.

delete.description: Remove an audit subscription and cancel queued deliveries. Requires audit_manage. An HTTP delivery already in flight cannot be recalled. The endpoint remains registered for other event types.

post.description: Replay a recorded delivery for the current audit subscription. Requires audit_manage. Source retention and the current action filter are checked again before sending. Expired or unsubscribed events are dropped.

Reissue a pending non-owner invitation with a live members_manage key. The old token is invalidated and the new token is returned once with renewed expiry. Its role and permissions are preserved. This operation does not prove email delivery and is not automatically retried.

get.description: Lists retained people in the key workspace and environment. Each returned person records a person.viewed audit event. Expired people are excluded before background deletion. email and phone narrow the list to people holding that exact address or number, so a client can open the person it already has instead of adding a duplicate.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Pass next_cursor from the prior page.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Return only people whose email is this address, compared without case or surrounding spaces.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: Return only people whose phone is this number, compared without surrounding spaces.

post.summary: Create or reuse a workspace person.
post.description: Creates a person. An explicit person_id or external_id reuses the named workspace person. A reference-only request keeps submitted details; identity supplied with that reference replaces those details. A shared email or phone only suggests a match. Suggested matches are returned only with people-read access. The workspace retention setting determines expires_at. An existing person keeps their original expiry. An Idempotency-Key returns the same retained person on retries, without creating another. Changed input with the same key answers 409 idempotency_key_reused. A customer reference that names another person or several people answers 409 person_reference_conflict.

get.description: Returns submitted details, the current retention expiry and the most recent retained completed or partial investigation evidence, together with retained follow-up search evidence. Migrated results whose original per-person status is unknown may also supply evidence. Earlier results and pending jobs remain available through investigation history; each investigation retains its own collected result. Full source records, posts and media are returned by default; explicit evidence.read denial withholds collected evidence and free-text notes. Each read records person.viewed without raw evidence in the audit log. A missing or expired person answers 404.

delete.description: Deletes a person and their retained evidence, and investigation history. Requires the separate delete permission. The audit retains only the person id and deletion metadata.

post.summary: Join one of a workspace person's records to them, or reject it.
post.description: Records a verdict on one of the records the person report holds: joined makes the record the person's whatever its likelihood, and rejected keeps it a lead that leads nowhere. The verdict belongs to the person on their own: the person report and enrichment follow it. It sticks for as long as the person's evidence holds the same record, and a later verdict on the same record replaces it. After each verdict, enrichment reads the person again under the environment's enrichment setting: it starts no search from a rejected record or from what a search of it found, and a joined record's values lead on. A record the person report does not hold answers 404. Each verdict is audited as person.record_judged. The decisions scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

post.summary: Search again on a value of one of a workspace person's records.
post.description: Starts a search on the person. The person's own enrichment then follows what it finds. Its records join the person report. Starts a new search on the value of one field of one of the person's records: a lookup's, a profile's or one an earlier search found. Name the record and the field; the value itself is not sent. The field's kind must be email, phone, username, person_name, password, hash, ip or domain. A domain search finds the breach rows of every email address at the domain, which must be a registrable domain or a host under one; any other domain answers 400. After a workspace person's investigation, while the environment's enrichment mode, or an investigation's override, is automatic, enrichment also starts searches by itself, with requested_by enrichment, on the distinctive values of the enrichment kinds (usernames by default; email addresses, phone numbers and person names when named) of records more likely than min_likelihood (0.5 by default) to be the person's: each value at most once per person (once more if that search failed), at most 5 searches from one search's records and 20 per person, at most 6 searches deep, within max_spend and the deadline when set, and within the screening cap; at the screening cap it waits and tries again later. A record a search finds starts from the likelihood of the record it came from, divided by one plus the results the search found on that site, or anywhere for a name search, so a chain grows less likely with each search and stops. In suggest mode enrichment starts none by itself, and the person report lists what it would start in suggested_searches. The search runs the breach search and the account and phone lookups that take the value's kind, under the environment's source controls, and finishes seconds later. A password or hash search counts first: it stops at counted with rows, how many breach rows hold the value, and runs only when a person runs it. Name a table, as a lookup remaining entry names it, to fetch the rows an earlier search left out, up to 100. What the search finds joins the person's lookup records as leads, each match naming the search; the person report lists the searches, each with the value and the record and field it came from, and its records are scored like the rest. Without an Idempotency-Key, starting the same open search returns it. Its estimate counts against the environment's screening_daily_cap, and one the cap cannot hold answers 409 screening_cap_exceeded. A record or field the person does not hold answers 404. Each search is audited as person.search_started. Send an Idempotency-Key to retry safely: the same key and request return the same resource in its current state while it is retained, even after work completes. Reusing the key with different input answers 409 idempotency_key_reused. Use a new key for a deliberate new operation. The investigations scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

post.summary: Run a counted password or hash search on a workspace person.
post.description: Runs a counted search that was started on the person (POST /v1/people/{person_id}/searches). Runs a password or hash search once a person has seen its count. A search still counting answers 409 group_conflict; one already queued, running or finished answers as it is. The body is an empty object. Its estimate counts against the environment's screening_daily_cap. Each run is audited as person.search_run. The investigations scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

get.description: List investigation history. The API key determines the workspace and environment.

post.summary: Start an investigation for a person.
post.description: Starts an investigation against a retained workspace person. enrichment overrides, field by field, how the environment's enrichment setting runs after this investigation; the person's latest investigation decides the enrichment that runs on them. Idempotency-Key is required: the same key and input return the same retained job in its current state without repeating billable work. Different input with that key answers 409 idempotency_key_reused; a deliberate new investigation uses a new key. The response includes Location and Retry-After. The person's retention expiry limits both execution and retained history. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

get.summary: Read an investigation and its evidence.
get.description: Returns this investigation's status, coverage, source records, posts and media. Full evidence is returned by default; explicit evidence.read denial keeps submitted person details, status and coverage, and hides collected evidence. The read is durably audited as person.viewed. The API key selects the workspace and environment. Missing, foreign or expired results answer 404.

post.description: Stops this investigation. A completed or already cancelled investigation keeps its current result. Other investigations for the person keep running.

post.summary: Mark a change on a workspace person reviewed.
post.description: Marks one change between a person's investigations reviewed, so it sorts below the unreviewed ones. Reviewing again keeps the first reviewer and time. Reviewing a change is not a decision on the person. The body is an empty object. Each review is audited as person.change_reviewed. The decisions scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions withhold before and after. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

Sets how often the person is investigated again: daily, weekly or monthly, counted from now, or off. Each due run starts one full investigation of the person, which the person's investigations list and whose changes the person report stores. Setting the period the schedule already has keeps its next run. The schedule lives in the database and the worker runs it, so a restart or a release neither skips nor repeats a run. Each change is audited as person.schedule_changed. The investigations scope grants this operation. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

apiKey.description: Your API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. A key selects one workspace environment. Each operation declares its required scope. People-read access includes evidence by default, subject to explicit evidence restrictions. Rotate with POST /v1/keys/rotate. A missing, malformed, revoked or expired key answers 401; a key without the operation's scope answers 403.

Access.description: public profiles were read; a private or locked one exists but could not be read.

Admission.description: immediate (the default): an assessment of this flow is decided from the evidence its answer has, and later evidence may change the decision. held: while the account's current assessment of this flow has not completed, the account's decision for the flow is held, and the final decision arrives as account.risk_changed when the investigation completes or hold_seconds pass, whichever is first. Each flow has its own admission.

AuditEvent.description: One privileged workspace action with its actor, target, outcome and time. Successful data changes commit their audit evidence atomically. Sensitive exports record access before returning bytes. Details exclude secrets and subject identifiers.

id.description: Opaque, server-assigned event id: aud_ and a 26-character ULID.

workspace_id.description: The workspace id, which is also its live environment's workspace id; the test environment's is the same id with :test appended. A workspace created through the API is tnt_ and a 26-character ULID.

environment.description: The affected live or test environment. Workspace-wide changes keep live here for compatibility; affected_environment identifies their workspace scope explicitly.

action.description: What happened, as resource.verb: workspace.created, member.role_changed, member.removed, invite.created, invite.revoked, invite.accepted, key.rotated, webhook_endpoint.created, webhook_endpoint.deleted, webhook_endpoint.secret_rotated, integration.created, integration.deleted, integration.secret_rotated, list_entry.created, list_entry.deleted, webhook_endpoint.test_sent, webhook_endpoint.verification_requested, webhook_endpoint.delivery_replayed, assessment.created, assessment.outcome_recorded, assessment.deleted, account.outcome_recorded, account.enforcement_recorded, account.deleted, account.exported. A change with no finer name carries the permission it used, such as keys.live.write. A member's read of raw evidence is breach_records.read or review_locations.read, with the assessment and counts and no value. New actions may appear; treat an unknown one as a change to its target.

outcome.description: succeeded: the change took effect. denied: an active member's role did not allow it, and nothing changed.

detail.description: At most 8 short facts about the change, keyed by lowercase names: the role a member was given or accepted (role), the invite an accepted member used (invite_id), the key that replaced a rotated one (new_key_id), the assessment a member's change acted on (assessment_id). Absent when there are none.

affected_environment.description: The affected scope, independent of the tenant partition storing the event. Workspace-wide membership and invitation changes use workspace.

request_id.description: Validated request correlation id, also returned in X-Request-ID, linking this event to request diagnostics. Absent on historical events without correlation.

id.description: The event id, equal to the NR-Webhook-Id header and across redeliveries and every endpoint the event fans out to.

created_at.description: When the event was created. Equal across redeliveries; the signing timestamp header is per delivery.

test.description: Present, and true, only on an event sent by POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/test: its data is a fixed example investigation, not one of the workspace's, so a receiver acknowledges it and applies nothing. Real events have no test member.

AuditEventList.description: GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit: one page of the workspace's audit log, both environments, newest first. Events are kept for as long as the workspace exists and are deleted with it. next_cursor is present only when another page exists.

workspace_id.description: The workspace id, which is also its live environment's workspace id; the test environment's is the same id with :test appended. A workspace created through the API is tnt_ and a 26-character ULID.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, MAC'd by the server and bound to the workspace it was issued for. Pass it back unchanged as cursor; a tampered, foreign or expired cursor answers 400 invalid_cursor.

type.description: The kind of resource the change acted on.

id.description: The resource's id, when it has one.

AuditEventTargetType.description: The kind of resource the change acted on.

event_id.description: Opaque, workspace-scoped webhook event id. A redelivery of the same event carries the same event_id, so consumers deduplicate on it.

AuthenticationErrorCode.description: Machine codes an HTTP 401 answer can carry.

BadRequestErrorCode.description: Machine codes an HTTP 400 answer can carry.

ConflictErrorCode.description: Machine codes an HTTP 409 answer can carry.

ConsoleLookups.description: The live environment's daily cap on assessments members make through the console (the playground), as spent on the current UTC day. Each console submission with a new Idempotency-Key spends one lookup; a replay spends nothing, and API keys and the test environment spend none. When used reaches limit, the next lookup answers 429 lookup_limit_reached until resets_at. The count is the one the cap enforces.

used.description: Lookups spent since the last reset.

resets_at.description: The next reset: the coming midnight UTC, when used returns to 0.

CustomerExportActionRequest.description: Send an empty JSON object to cancel or retry a customer export.

data.description: Base64-encoded UTF-8 JSON Lines, at most 256 KiB decoded. Each line is a typed customer export record. Decode and concatenate chunks in index order within the same generation.

account_id.description: Your own opaque identifier for the account being checked, scoped to your workspace. Use an id you mint, with no direct identifier (email, phone, name or national id) in it. '|' is accepted so an Auth0 user id such as 'auth0|64abc' passes unchanged; '@', '+', '$' and whitespace are refused by the pattern, as is an exact-shape JWT; a hex digest such as a SHA-256 is allowed, because hashing an internal id is a common pseudonymous scheme. A value such as '07700900123' or 'jane.doe.gmail.com' cannot be told apart from an opaque id. It travels in bodies, and in a URL only as the path segment of GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}, its /assessments and its /links. An assessment requested by a provider hook at pre_registration, which has no account yet, carries the server-issued account_id pre: followed by its assessment_id.

Depth.description: standard reads the bio and the last 100 posts of each profile.

endpoint_id.description: Opaque id of the endpoint registration being verified.

challenge.description: Endpoint verification nonce: 32 random bytes, unpadded base64url (43 characters). Fresh per verification.

id.description: The event id, equal to the NR-Webhook-Id header and across redeliveries and every endpoint the event fans out to.

created_at.description: When the event was created. Equal across redeliveries; the signing timestamp header is per delivery.

test.description: Present, and true, only on an event sent by POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/test: its data is a fixed example investigation, not one of the workspace's, so a receiver acknowledges it and applies nothing. Real events have no test member.

Enrichment.description: How enrichment searches the values that a workspace person's investigation (POST /v1/investigations) finds. Defaults: mode automatic, min_likelihood 0.5, kinds username, max_spend null and deadline null. An investigation request may override each field for that investigation. A change applies to the next search enrichment starts, investigations already run included. Enrichment also keeps to limits of its own: each value once per person (once more if that search failed), at most 5 searches from one search's records, 20 per person and 6 searches deep.

min_likelihood.description: Enrichment searches values only from records more likely than this to be the person's, 0 to 0.99.

kinds.description: The kinds of value enrichment searches: distinctive usernames, email addresses and phone numbers, which belong to one person each, and distinctive person names, searched in the breach data.

max_spend.description: The most enrichment may spend on a person from one investigation, in minor units of USD (cents): each search it started after that investigation started counts its estimate or what it spent, whichever is more. At the bound enrichment starts nothing more for that investigation. null: only the environment's screening_daily_cap bounds it.

deadline.description: How long enrichment may start searches after an investigation starts, 60 to 2592000 seconds. null: no deadline.

EnrichmentChange.description: A change to enrichment. A field left out keeps the value in force; max_spend or deadline null removes the bound.

min_likelihood.description: Enrichment searches values only from records more likely than this to be the person's, 0 to 0.99.

kinds.description: The kinds of value enrichment searches: distinctive usernames, email addresses and phone numbers, which belong to one person each, and distinctive person names, searched in the breach data.

max_spend.description: The most enrichment may spend on a person from one investigation, in minor units of USD (cents): each search it started after that investigation started counts its estimate or what it spent, whichever is more. At the bound enrichment starts nothing more for that investigation. null: only the environment's screening_daily_cap bounds it.

deadline.description: How long enrichment may start searches after an investigation starts, 60 to 2592000 seconds. null: no deadline.

EnrichmentMode.description: off: enrichment starts no search and suggests none. suggest: enrichment starts no search by itself, and the person report lists the searches it would start in suggested_searches. automatic: after a workspace person's investigation, and each time a search on that person finishes, enrichment starts searches by itself.

ErasureReceipt.description: Acknowledged propagation of a retained erasure record in the calling environment. Pending means the target has not acknowledged completion. Completion covers these serving-system targets only; backup and point-in-time recovery copies expire according to their own retention policy. This receipt contains no subject id or digest. Workspace teardown revokes customer credentials, so obtain required receipts before teardown.

id.description: Opaque, server-issued erasure receipt id. It contains no subject identifier.

backup_policy.example: Backups expire under the documented backup retention policy.

ErrorCode.description: Why a failed search found nothing: its sources did not answer, none could be asked, or it could not run before its attempts were spent.

Failure.description: Why the attempt failed: the URL is no longer valid, the host did not resolve, it resolved to an address that is not public, no answer within 5 seconds, the connection failed, a 3xx (redirects are not followed) or another non-2xx status. Absent for a delivered attempt.

FlowChange.description: A change to one flow. A field left out keeps the value in force. Thresholds set on login or purchase start from the values in force, account_creation's while it inherits them. After the change, 0 < step_up < review <= 100 and block is off or review <= block <= 100.

block.description: The score from which the decision is block; null turns blocking off.

inherits_account_creation.description: Login or purchase only: drop the flow's own thresholds so it uses account_creation's again. Not combined with step_up, review or block. Send true; false is refused.

inherits_signup.description: Alias of inherits_account_creation, still accepted. Send true; false is refused.

hold_seconds.description: How long a held flow's assessment is held after it was created, 30 to 86400 seconds (default 300). Kept while the flow is immediate.

FlowSettings.description: One flow's policy in force. A score below step_up is allow, below review step_up, and from review review; from block, when present, the decision is block. admission says when the flow's decision is final.

block.description: The score from which the decision is block. Absent while blocking is off, the default.

default_depth.description: The depth a request for this flow that names none is served at. Defaults: full for account_creation and purchase, quick for login.

inherits_account_creation.description: true while this flow has no thresholds of its own and uses account_creation's, the default for login and purchase. Always false for signup.

hold_seconds.description: How long a held flow's assessment is held after it was created, 30 to 86400 seconds (default 300). Kept while the flow is immediate.

A service key outlives its creator; a personal key belongs to the authenticated member and is revoked on membership or authority changes. request_id deduplicates creation: retry returns 200 metadata without the secret; changed parameters answer 409. Team scopes members and members_manage are explicitly workspace-wide, live-only, and delegated by a current full owner. Personal credentials cannot hold management or members_manage. Legacy management includes policy publication; use settings without policy_publish for configuration preparation and retention-only edits.

ProfileMatchState.description: How sure the screening is that a profile is the person's, from the likelihood its record scores. Confirmed reaches the join bar of 0.9. Probable reaches 0.85, which takes a shared value beyond the one that found the account. Possible is the rest.

Publication.description: Immutable publication provenance remains in policy history after evaluation evidence expires. SHA-256 values identify the frozen manifest, evaluator semantic input, cohort, and canonical result separately.

RateLimitErrorCode.description: Machine codes an HTTP 429 answer can carry.

Rating.description: unique: an email or phone, which belongs to one person by design. distinctive: rare enough that a new search on it likely finds one person. common: shared by many people, so a search on it finds strangers. A new search is suggested for unique and distinctive values only; any value can still be searched.

id.description: Made from the source and the fields' names and original values, so the same answer found twice is one record with the same id. Its fields are typed as its latest finding typed them.

source.description: Where the record came from: the connector, the kind of source and the site, and for a leaked row its table and date.

matched.description: Each kind of searched value that found the record.

fields.description: Every field the source returned, in the order the source's connector lists them; a breach row's columns in name order. Nothing is withheld: a breach row's passwords, hashes and salts are fields like any other.

observed_at.description: When the source last gave this answer.

likelihood.description: How likely the record is the person it was found for, from 0.01 to 0.99, to two places. A record found by the person's own email or phone starts as theirs, and one found by a search of a value another record holds starts at that record's likelihood divided by one plus the records its search found on its site; any other starts lower the more people its search found on its site, or anywhere for a name search. Each value it shares with what is known of the person raises it, a rare value more than a common one, and a different birth date or full name lowers it. What is known is what the person's row gives and the values of their joined records: those found by their email or phone, those a reviewer joined and those whose likelihood reaches 0.9. Each record that joins adds its values and the rest are scored again until the joined records stop changing; a record whose likelihood falls below 0.9 is not joined and adds nothing, so a reviewer's rejection also undoes the joins that came through the rejected record. A record whose source kind starts with domain_ describes an email's domain, not the person, so it is not compared and adds nothing to what is known: it stays at 0.99 when the person's own email found it and at 0.5 otherwise. Present on a person's lookup records, with agreed, clashed and joined.

agreed.description: The fields of this record whose values agreed with what is known of the person, by their field names, in the record's order. The value that found the record is not among them.

clashed.description: The fields of this record that clashed with what is known of the person: a birth date or a full name that differs from the person's.

joined.description: Whether the record joins the person: its likelihood reached 0.9 or a reviewer joined it, and no reviewer rejected it. A record that does not join stays a lead.

verdict.description: A reviewer's overrule (POST .../people/{person_id}/records), which decides joined whatever the likelihood and sticks for as long as a lookup finds the same record. Absent when nobody overruled it.

evidence.description: Why the record has its likelihood, as the items that make it up: what found it and each value it agrees or clashes with, each with its weight in bits. The bits add up to the likelihood before rounding: likelihood = 1 / (1 + 2^-sum). Only the strongest agreement of each kind counts, and a place counts once however many of its city, region, country and address agree. Present on a person's lookup records that have any such item.

path.description: How the record connects to what the investigator gave: given first, then the ids of the joined records it reached the person through, nearest last. Each step follows what found the record before the strongest agreement. A record with no link to the person has no path.

other_person.description: For a record that is not the person's, the other person it belongs with: records that share this number share strong values, such as an email or a full name with a phone, and score as one person against each other. Absent on the person's own records and on a record that matches nobody else. A value that more than 20 strangers hold groups nobody, and a record that agrees with what you sent has none.

Record.description: One answer from one source: where it came from, what found it and every field it holds. A person's lookup records also say how likely each is the person.

signal.description: anchors_disagree: records found by two of the identifiers you gave clash with each other, so those identifiers may belong to different people.

kind.description: The kind of value that clashes: person_name or born.

between.description: The two identifiers you gave whose records disagree.

records.description: The ids of the two records that clash, in the order of between.

RecordConflict.description: Two identifiers you gave that lead to records of different people.

rating.description: unique: an email or phone, which belongs to one person by design. distinctive: rare enough that a new search on it likely finds one person. common: shared by many people, so a search on it finds strangers. A new search is suggested for unique and distinctive values only; any value can still be searched.

reason.description: Why, in plain words, such as "seen 3,861,493 times in breach data", "in 4 breach rows" or "38 bits, about one in 430 billion usernames".

rows.description: How many breach rows hold the value, when they were counted. Set for a username, password, hash or person name.

pwned.description: How many times the Pwned Passwords list holds the password, when it was asked. Set for a password only.

bits.description: How surprising the username is, to one decimal place: a character model spells it about once in 2^bits usernames. Set for a username the model can spell.

RecordDistinctive.description: How distinctive a searchable value is: an email, phone, username, password, hash, person name or IP. Absent for other values, for a field with no value, and when its rating could not be worked out, such as when a count failed. Linkage weighs a password, hash or username by these numbers: the rarer the value, the more a shared one counts.

signal.description: found_by: what found the record, which sets where its likelihood starts. agrees: a value the record shares with what the investigator gave or with a joined record. clashes: a birth date, full name, gender or country that differs from theirs.

kind.description: For found_by, what the search looked up (email, phone, username, handle, name). Otherwise the kind of value compared, such as email, username, person_name, born, city or crypto_address.

field.description: The record's own field that agreed or clashed, or for found_by the field the search matched.

with.description: given for what the investigator gave, or the id of the person's record it agreed or clashed with, or for found_by the record whose value the search looked up.

with_field.description: The field on the other side: the field of the given identity or of the record named by with.

bits.description: The item's weight in bits, to two places: log2 of how much likelier the evidence is for the same person than for a stranger. Positive raises the likelihood and negative lowers it.

RecordEvidence.description: One item of evidence behind a record's likelihood.

RecordEvidenceSignal.description: found_by: what found the record, which sets where its likelihood starts. agrees: a value the record shares with what the investigator gave or with a joined record. clashes: a birth date, full name, gender or country that differs from theirs.

field.description: The source's own name for the field. A nested value's name is dotted, and a list element's carries its index.

original.description: The value as the source wrote it. A count is written in decimal and a time in RFC 3339; a breach column's value is as the leak holds it.

kind.description: What sort of value the field holds, which decides the form of value.

role.description: Which common field the value is, where many sources share it. Absent for a field only its source returns.

value.description: The value cleaned to its kind's one form: an email in lower case, a phone number in international form when its country is known, a date in ISO form, a country as its two-letter code, a flag as true or false. Absent when the value cannot be cleaned as its kind, or when the source masked it or cut it short, with a run of asterisks or bullets or a trailing ellipsis, in a kind that links people or is searched again; original still holds it.

detail.description: What the value shows of itself beyond its kind: the likely algorithm of a hash, the likely coin of a crypto address or the currency of an amount.

distinctive.description: How distinctive a searchable value is, so whether a new search on it would find one person.

noise.description: True when the value tells an investigator nothing on its own: a setting flag, a zero count, a bare number or a value with no letter or digit, in a field with no role. A field with a role is not noise. Investigation views hide noise by default; the field is still returned in full.

x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.email: An email address. value: in lower case, without a mailto: prefix.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.phone: A phone number. value: in E.164 form, such as +447700900123. A national number is cleaned only when the country of the source's site is known.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.username: A handle a person chose. value: as written. Compare it in lower case. A value that is only zeros, or null, nil, none, undefined or n/a, has no value.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.account_id: A platform's own id for an account. value: as written. A value that is only zeros, or null, nil, none, undefined or n/a, has no value.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.url: A web address. value: the scheme and host in lower case, the path, query and fragment as written.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.domain: A host name with no path. value: in lower case, also when the source wrote a URL.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.image: A picture, as a link or a file. value: the link, cleaned as a `url`, else the file as written. A value that is only zeros, or null, nil, none, undefined or n/a, has no value.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.person_name: A whole name or a part of one. value: with each run of spaces made one space.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.gender: A stated gender. value: `female`, `male` or `other` when the value names one of them, else as written.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.age: An age in years. value: a whole number from 0 to 150.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.language: A language. value: its ISO 639 code, two letters when the language has them.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.organisation: A company, school or group by name. value: with each run of spaces made one space.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.job_title: A position or occupation. value: as written.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.country: A country. value: its ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, such as GB.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.region: A state, province or county. value: as written.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.city: A city or town. value: as written.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.address: A street address or one line of it. value: as written. A value that is only zeros, or null, nil, none, undefined or n/a, has no value.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.postcode: A postal code. value: in upper case with single spaces.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.coordinates: A latitude and longitude. value: `latitude,longitude` in decimal degrees.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.timezone: A timezone or an offset. value: an IANA zone name, UTC, or an offset such as +05:30.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.date: A calendar date. value: in ISO form at the precision the source gives: 2014, 2014-03 or 2014-03-07.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.date_time: A moment. value: in ISO form in UTC, such as 2014-03-07T09:30:00Z, or a date when the source gives no time.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.duration: A length of time. value: a number of seconds.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.ip: An IPv4 or IPv6 address. value: its standard text form. An IPv4 address stored as a whole number is written as IPv4.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.mac_address: A network card address. value: in lower case with colons.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.device_id: An id of a phone, computer or browser. value: as written. A value that is only zeros, or null, nil, none, undefined or n/a, has no value.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.user_agent: A browser or app signature. value: as written.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.password: A password in plain text. value: exactly as written, spaces included.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.hash: A password hash. value: as written. detail names the likely algorithm, such as bcrypt.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.salt: The salt for a hash. value: exactly as written.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.token: A session, reset or API token. value: as written. A value that is only zeros, or null, nil, none, undefined or n/a, has no value.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.security_answer: A security question or its answer. value: exactly as written.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.card_number: A payment card number. value: its 12 to 19 digits only.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.bank_account: An IBAN or account number. value: its letters and digits only, in upper case.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.crypto_address: A wallet address. value: as written. detail names the likely coin, such as BTC.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.amount: Money, with its currency when given. value: a plain decimal. detail names the currency, such as USD.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.id_number: A passport, tax, national or licence number. value: as written. A value that is only zeros, or null, nil, none, undefined or n/a, has no value.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.vehicle: A number plate or a VIN. value: in upper case with no spaces.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.label: One of a small set, such as a status or level. value: as written.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.long_text: Free writing, such as a bio or signature. value: as written.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.count: A whole number of things. value: a whole number of 0 or more, with no thousands separators.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.score: A rating, rank or points. value: a plain decimal.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.flag: A yes or no. value: `true` or `false`.
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.structured: A nested value that could not be split. value: as written.

RecordKind.description: What sort of value a field holds, which decides how it is cleaned, compared and searched again. It comes from the source where the source declares it, as a connector does for the fields it states, else from the value itself where its shape is certain (an email, an IP, a URL, an international phone number), else from the answer committed for the source's column, else from the answer stored for it, else text. A value of any kind is returned. Each kind's description says what it holds and the form value takes.

by.description: The kind of searched value: email, phone, username, ip, name, password, hash, domain, or handle for a profile read of a handle.

field.description: The field the searched value hit, when the record holds it.

search.description: The search a person started on a value of another record that found this one, among the person report's searches, which names the value and the record and field it came from. A record found only by such searches is a lead, whatever kind of value found it. Absent for a match of the lookups.

RecordMatch.description: One searched value that found the record.

source.description: The source whose rows the search matched: for a leaked row, its table.

by.description: The kind of searched value whose search matched the rows, as a record's matched names it.

search.description: The search a person started that matched the rows. Searching the same field again with this source's table fetches them.

rows.description: How many rows of the source that search matched beyond the records the lookup carries.

RecordRemaining.description: Rows one search matched in one source that the lookup's records leave out, so no answer is cut short in silence.

x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.account_status: The state of the account, such as active or suspended (`label`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.account_type: The sort of account, such as personal or business (`label`).

x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.bio: What the person wrote about themselves (`long_text`).

x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.cover_picture: The banner picture of the profile (`image`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.declines: How many of the account's payments a shop declined (`count`).

x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.email_verified: Whether the site verified the email (`flag`).

x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.followers: How many accounts follow the account (`count`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.following: How many accounts the account follows (`count`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.friends: How many friends the account has (`count`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.full_address: A whole postal address on one line (`address`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.headline: A headline or user title shown with the name (`text`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.job_title: A job title the source states (`job_title`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.joined: When the account was made (`date` or `date_time`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.last_active: When the account was last active (`date` or `date_time`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.last_ip: The IP the account last used (`ip`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.last_post: When the account last posted (`date` or `date_time`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.last_updated: When the account or its profile last changed (`date` or `date_time`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.level: A level or rank on the site (`label`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.likes_given: How many likes the account gave (`count`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.likes_received: How many likes the account received (`count`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.line_type: The line type of a phone number, such as mobile or VoIP (`label`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.linked_account: An account on another network. The field's name names the network (`username`, `account_id` or `url`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.location: A place as the person wrote it (`text`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.marked_spam: Whether callers mark a phone number as spam (`flag`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.organisation: An organisation the source names, such as a company (`organisation`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.other_ip: An IP whose use the source does not say (`ip`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.paid: Whether the account is paid or premium (`flag`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.password_changed: When the password last changed (`date` or `date_time`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.payment_method: The payment method or card brand the account paid with (`label`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.posts: How many posts the account made (`count`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.profile_views: How many times people viewed the profile (`count`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.referrals: How many people the account referred (`count`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.referrer: Who or what referred the account (`text`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.report_count: How many reports callers made on a phone number (`count`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.reputation_label: A reputation label for a phone number (`label`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.residence: The country the person lives in (`country`).
