x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.street: A street line of an address (`address`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.trades: How many trades a forum account completed (`count`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.verified: Whether the site verified the account (`flag`).
x-noresponse-enum-descriptions.warnings: Warnings and infractions on the account (`count`).

RecordRole.description: Which common field a value is, where many sources share it: a join date and a birth date are both dates, with the roles joined and born. A platform account's field and a breach row's column with the same meaning carry the same kind and role. A linked_account field is named by its network. Absent for a field only its source returns. Each role's description names the kinds its values have.

connector.description: The id of the connector that read the record: breach for a breach row.

kind.description: The kind of source: platform for an account read off a live platform; for a breach row, the kind of leak its table is: site_breach, credential_list, stealer_log, scrape, hacking_forum, abuse_service or darkweb_site; domain_registry for an email domain's registry record and domain_dns for its mail records.

site.description: The host a person knows the source's site by.

table.description: The table a leaked row came from.

date.description: When the source's data dates from, at the precision it is known: YYYY or YYYY-MM for a breach table, and YYYY-MM-DD, the day the computer was infected, for a row of a stealer log.

RecordVerdict.description: A recorded verdict on one record. A later verdict on the same record replaces it.

record_id.description: One of the person's lookup records.

verdict.description: joined: the record is the person's, whatever its likelihood. rejected: the record stays a lead, whatever its likelihood.

RecordVerdictRequest.description: A reviewer's verdict on whether one of a person's lookup records is theirs.

RequestAggregateRequest.description: Count every retained matching attempt in [from,to). Capture is best effort; missing attempts cannot be inferred. UTC buckets may be partial at the edges. The window is at most 7 days.

RequestDiagnostic.description: One authenticated HTTP attempt. An attempt id is independent of the caller correlation id. No raw body, path parameter, credential or source payload is retained. write_complete means the server wrote/flushed its response, not proof the client processed it. Collection is bounded best effort; ii_signup_request_diagnostic_failures_total exposes gaps. Retained for seven days or the shorter environment retention.

api_key_id.description: Public authenticated API key identifier. Absent for member requests and older unattributed diagnostics.

RequestDiagnosticPage.description: Authenticated attempts in a bounded interval, newest first. Keep the same filters when paging.

ResponseMode.description: The response mode recorded for the endpoint: standard (the default) or detailed, which needs an API key with the detailed scope as well. No event the API sends today differs by mode.

Role.description: A built-in capability set. Specialist roles are independent; effective access is returned by GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/capabilities.

SchedulePeriod.description: How often the person is investigated again: daily, weekly or monthly, counted from when the schedule was set; off runs no scheduled investigation.

period_from.description: The oldest item read on any platform.

period_to.description: The newest item read on any platform.

items.description: A platform a screening can cover, such as instagram, x, bluesky, youtube, tiktok or github. The screening registry owns the set: a request that names a platform it does not cover answers 422. A new platform adds an id without changing this contract, so read a platform you do not know in a response as one you have not seen before, not as an error. synthetic is the deterministic connector's own platform, for exercising the product end to end with no network.

not_searched.description: Requested platforms where the person gave the screening nothing to look up, such as no handle for a platform that reads supplied handles only. Nothing looked and nothing failed: such a platform is not in platforms, is not none_found and does not make the person partial.

sources.description: How many sources this search asked and how many answered, across the lookup stage (sources asked whether an account exists for an identifier) and the platform stage (profiles read on each platform). A source that answered may have found nothing; one that did not answer failed or ran out of time.

timing.description: How long this search's latest attempt took, stage by stage. started_at minus the investigation's creation is the time spent queued or retrying.

ScreeningCoverage.description: The denominator of a screening: accounts found, how many could be read, items read and the period they span, so a clean result is distinct from a person nobody could see.

ScreeningCoverageSources.description: How many sources this search asked and how many answered, across the lookup stage (sources asked whether an account exists for an identifier) and the platform stage (profiles read on each platform). A source that answered may have found nothing; one that did not answer failed or ran out of time.

answered.description: Lookup sources plus platforms that answered.

lookups.description: The sum of sources and answered over lookup.checks.

platforms.description: Entries of platforms, and those whose status is covered, none_found or inaccessible.

ScreeningCoverageTiming.description: How long this search's latest attempt took, stage by stage. started_at minus the investigation's creation is the time spent queued or retrying.

started_at.description: When the attempt that wrote this result started.

total_ms.description: Milliseconds from started_at to the end of the last stage listed.

stages.description: Stages finished so far, in order. The result first written lists stages up to written; the settled result lists them all.

checks.description: Each lane each identifier was looked up in, identifiers in the order email, phone, username and lanes in the order accounts, phone, breach, domain. Every lane the person's identifiers are looked up in is listed: one that no source answered, or that no source could be asked in, is not_covered. Empty when the person has no email, phone or handle to look up.

answers.description: Each source asked, with what it answered and when. answered_at is absent while the source has not answered.

records.description: What each source answered, whole, each answer once: every field of each account a connector found, and every column of each breach row the person's email or usernames matched, under the source's own names, and what each search a person started found, each match naming its search. Anyone who may read the person reads them: no extra permission applies, breach passwords and hashes included.

remaining.description: For each search and source whose matched rows records leave out, how many: a breach search returns at most 20 rows of a table and 100 in all, from its first 64 tables by name. A search a person starts on one table of its source fetches the rest of that table, up to 100 rows. Absent when records hold every matched row.

conflicts.description: Identifiers you gave that lead to different people. Absent when they agree.

ScreeningLookup.description: What the signup check's lookups found for a person: account presence for the email, phone and usernames (the person's handles), the phone lookup, the email domain's registration and the breach search. Nothing here sets a match state.

connector.description: The id of the connector asked: breach for the breach search.

status.description: found: a source found the identifier. not_found: every source answered and none found it. partial: the sources that answered found nothing and the others did not answer. not_covered: no source answered. A lookup that failed reads partial or not_covered, not not_found.

sources.description: Sources asked: none when no source could be, as when the source is stopped or your workspace refuses it.

answered.description: Sources that gave a definite answer.

reason.description: Why a source did not answer, or none could be asked: the lane's most specific failure, or insufficient_evidence when every source that did not answer could not tell (inconclusive). A lane with a reason reads partial or not_covered.

unanswered.description: Each source that did not give a definite answer, by connector, with why: the same connector id a record's source names. A source of the lane that no connector covers is counted in sources and not named here.

ScreeningLookupCheck.description: What came of one lane of the lookups for one identifier.

ScreeningLookupCheckStatus.description: found: a source found the identifier. not_found: every source answered and none found it. partial: the sources that answered found nothing and the others did not answer. not_covered: no source answered. A lookup that failed reads partial or not_covered, not not_found.

connector.description: The id of the connector that did not answer: breach for the breach search.

ScreeningMatch.description: How a profile was matched to the person: the state its evidence earns, and the evidence.

kind.description: What matched. email, phone, supplied_handle and source_fact are hard identifiers; company, city and school are soft. supplied_handle is a handle on the person row; supplied_username is an account at the person's platform-free username, which alone makes a possible match; source_fact is an account a profile found by the person's lookups lists.

detail.description: Where the match was seen, such as the profile field that carried it.
detail.example: the email on the person's row

resolver.description: The resolver or collector that produced a record, by its catalogue name.

ScreeningMatchEvidence.description: One identifier that ties a profile to the person.

ScreeningMatchEvidenceKind.description: What matched. email, phone, supplied_handle and source_fact are hard identifiers; company, city and school are soft. supplied_handle is a handle on the person row; supplied_username is an account at the person's platform-free username, which alone makes a possible match; source_fact is an account a profile found by the person's lookups lists.

media_url.description: Where the platform serves the image or video.

cover_of.description: For an image that is a video's cover frame, the id of that video's media item.

screenshot_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the screenshot taken of a flagged item.

ScreeningMedia.description: One image or video a collector read, with the post that carried it.

platform.description: A platform a screening can cover, such as instagram, x, bluesky, youtube, tiktok or github. The screening registry owns the set: a request that names a platform it does not cover answers 422. A new platform adds an id without changing this contract, so read a platform you do not know in a response as one you have not seen before, not as an error. synthetic is the deterministic connector's own platform, for exercising the product end to end with no network.

status.description: covered read at least one profile; none_found looked and found no account; inaccessible found accounts that are private or locked; failed could not finish looking; unavailable has no resolver or collector enabled.

accounts_found.description: Accounts found on the platform: at most 5, the best candidates the search kept.

ScreeningPlatformCoverage.description: What a screening read on one platform.

ScreeningPlatformCoverageStatus.description: covered read at least one profile; none_found looked and found no account; inaccessible found accounts that are private or locked; failed could not finish looking; unavailable has no resolver or collector enabled.

text.example: Great coffee this morning before the commute.

repost_of.description: The permalink of the post this one reposts. text then holds that post's author's words, not the person's.

quote_of.description: The permalink of the post this one quotes. text holds the person's own words alone.

place.description: Where the post says it was made.

tagged.description: The handles of the accounts the post tags, on its own platform.

likes.description: How many likes the platform shows for the post.

comments.description: How many comments the platform shows for the post.

views.description: How many views or plays the platform shows for the post.

shares.description: How many times the platform shows the post was shared or reposted.

language.description: The language the platform says the post is in, as the platform codes it, such as en or pt-BR.

edited.description: true when the platform marks the post as edited after it went up. Absent when it does not mark it.

sponsored.description: true when the platform marks the post as a paid partnership or an ad. Absent when it does not mark it.

ai_generated.description: true when the platform labels the post as made or changed with AI. Absent when it does not label it.

posted_with.description: The app or device the platform says the post was made with.

stated.description: Everything else the platform sent about the post, under the platform's own names and as it typed them: counts, ids of linked posts and accounts, links, media details, labels and notices. The fields above are not repeated here. Nothing that describes the account the screening read with, such as whether it liked or saved the post, is ever here.

screenshot_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the screenshot taken of a flagged item.

ScreeningPost.description: One post a collector read, with its permalink and time.

platform.description: A platform a screening can cover, such as instagram, x, bluesky, youtube, tiktok or github. The screening registry owns the set: a request that names a platform it does not cover answers 422. A new platform adds an id without changing this contract, so read a platform you do not know in a response as one you have not seen before, not as an error. synthetic is the deterministic connector's own platform, for exercising the product end to end with no network.

bio.example: Engineer at Example Ltd in Melbourne.

access.description: public profiles were read; a private or locked one exists but could not be read.

collector.description: The resolver or collector that produced a record, by its catalogue name.

posts_stopped.description: Why fewer posts were read than the screening's depth asks for while the account holds more. platform_limit: the platform shows the screening no more of them. page_limit: the pages a screening reads ran out first. rate_limited or unavailable: a later page was held back or failed; the posts before it are kept and the person is partial. Absent when the account was read to its end or to the depth.

record.description: Everything the connector read of the account, whole, under the platform's own names. The fields above are the parts of it the roster shows. Absent from a profile screened before records were kept.

ScreeningProfile.description: An account the screening matched to the person, how it was matched, and how much of it was read.

ScreeningSpend.description: What screening cost, in US cents, in total and per implementation.

implementation.description: The resolver or collector that produced a record, by its catalogue name.

role.description: What the implementation did. analyser appears only on spend recorded before the engine stopped analysing posts.

ScreeningSpendLineRole.description: What the implementation did. analyser appears only on spend recorded before the engine stopped analysing posts.

record_id.description: The record whose value led to the search.

field.description: The field of that record that holds the value.

table.description: The one breach table searched, when the search was of one table.

kind.description: The kind of the value searched. A domain search finds the leaked rows of every email address at the domain.

value.description: The searched value. Empty in person reports when evidence.read is denied.

status.description: A password or hash search is counting, then counted: rows says how many breach rows hold the value, and nothing runs until a person runs it (POST .../searches/{search_id}/run). Any other search is queued, then running. completed: every source it asked answered. partial: some did not. failed: none answered or none could be asked, which says nothing about whether the value is held anywhere.

rows.description: How many breach rows hold the password or hash, counted before the search runs.

sources.description: How many sources the search asked: the breach search and the account and phone lookups that take the value's kind.

answered.description: How many of them gave a definite answer, found or not found.

found.description: How many records the search found. They are among the person report's lookup records, each match naming this search.

estimated_spend.description: What the search may spend, in US cents, held against the environment's daily screening cap while it runs.

spent.description: What the search spent, in US cents, metered as screening work.

error_code.description: Why a failed search found nothing: its sources did not answer, none could be asked, or it could not run before its attempts were spent.

requested_by.description: Who started the search: the member or key, or enrichment when the engine started it on a value an earlier result showed.

parent_search_id.description: The search that found the record this value came from. Absent when the record came from the person's investigation.

depth.description: How many searches lie between the person's investigation and this one, this one included: 1 for a value of a record the investigation found, 2 for a value of a record a depth-1 search found, and so on.

Search.description: One search on a value of one of a person's records, started by a person or by enrichment.

SearchKind.description: The kind of the value searched. A domain search finds the leaked rows of every email address at the domain.

record_id.description: One of the person's records: a lookup's, a profile's or one an earlier search found.

field.description: The name of the record's field whose value to search. Its kind must be email, phone, username, person_name, password, hash, ip or domain, and it must have a value: a field the source masked or that could not be cleaned is not searched.

table.description: Search only this breach table, as a remaining entry names it, to fetch the rows an earlier search left out. Not for a phone.

SearchRequest.description: The value to search again, named by the record and field that hold it rather than sent again.

SearchStatus.description: A password or hash search is counting, then counted: rows says how many breach rows hold the value, and nothing runs until a person runs it (POST .../searches/{search_id}/run). Any other search is queued, then running. completed: every source it asked answered. partial: some did not. failed: none answered or none could be asked, which says nothing about whether the value is held anywhere.

name.description: The NoResponse service that made the change with no person acting, such as replenisher, which replaces dead platform sessions in NoResponse's own workspace.

Settings.description: One environment's settings: how long its assessments are kept, and for each flow the risk thresholds that decide it and the depth a request that names none is served at, the sources it refuses, the daily cap on screening spend, and how enrichment searches what an investigation finds. Live and test each have their own. A flow without thresholds of its own uses account_creation's (inherits_account_creation). Every change is recorded in the audit log as settings.updated, with who made it.

workspace_id.description: The workspace id, which is also its live environment's workspace id; the test environment's is the same id with :test appended. A workspace created through the API is tnt_ and a 26-character ULID.

retention_days.description: Days an assessment is kept after it is created, 1 to 365 (default 365). Shortening hides older assessments at once.

policy_version.description: The monotonic settings configuration epoch, including retention changes. Zero while defaults apply. Historical assessments keep their frozen policy version; the active version reaches new assessments within a minute.

updated_by.description: Who last changed the policy: the member's external user id for a change made through the console, the prefix (nrk_<environment>_<key id>) of the management key that made it, or NoResponse. Absent while the defaults apply.

updated_at.description: When the policy last changed. Absent while the defaults apply.

items.description: A connector id a signup assessment may call, such as github, phone, breach, rdap, mx, ipintel, or a platform searched by email address, phone number or username. The connector registry owns the set: a request that names an id it does not declare for signup answers 422. A new source adds an id without changing this contract, so read an id you do not know in a response as a source you have not seen before, not as an error.

refused_sources.description: The sources this environment refuses, sorted; empty, the default, refuses none. An assessment leaves a refused source out: its coverage is missing (an identifier with no other source lists coverage-unavailable as unavailable) rather than not_found, and a stored result of a refused source is not reused.

screening_daily_cap.description: The most the environment's screenings may spend in one UTC day, in minor units of USD (cents), 0 to 100000000; null is no cap. Default 50000. A screening whose estimated_spend exceeds the cap less the day's recorded spend and what open screenings may still spend answers 409 screening_cap_exceeded.

SettingsRequest.description: Changes only named settings, atomically. Every successful write advances policy_version and retains an immutable settings snapshot. expected_policy_version optionally guards against stale edits; restore always requires it.

items.description: A connector id a signup assessment may call, such as github, phone, breach, rdap, mx, ipintel, or a platform searched by email address, phone number or username. The connector registry owns the set: a request that names an id it does not declare for signup answers 422. A new source adds an id without changing this contract, so read an id you do not know in a response as a source you have not seen before, not as an error.

refused_sources.description: Replaces the refused sources; [] refuses none. A change applies to new assessments within a minute.

screening_daily_cap.description: Replaces the daily screening cap, in minor units of USD; null removes the cap. Needs settings.write only, like retention_days.

enrichment.description: Changes how enrichment runs, field by field. Needs settings.write only, like retention_days.

flows.description: Use account_creation or its deprecated alias signup, not both.

expected_policy_version.description: Compare-and-set guard. A stale version returns 409 policy_version_conflict before any change; every settings write including retention advances the version.

change_reason.example: Adjust thresholds after reviewing retained evidence

SettingsRequestFlows.description: Use account_creation or its deprecated alias signup, not both.

SignalOutcome.description: Per-signal outcome. A source that timed out, was blocked or errored reports blocked, unavailable or inconclusive with a reason and is listed in incomplete_sources; not_found is a definite absence.

Significance.description: One rule ranks every change: identity changes (accounts, breaches, identifiers) are high, profile fields are medium, new posts are low.

secret.description: The signing secret: 32 random bytes as 43 characters of unpadded base64url. It is not stored in readable form or returned again.

field.description: The field of that record that holds the value. Send record_id and field to POST .../searches to start the search.

kind.description: The kind of the value: one of the kinds the environment's enrichment setting names.

likelihood.description: The likelihood of the record that holds the value, from 0.01 to 0.99. Enrichment suggests a value only from a record more likely than the setting's min_likelihood, the likeliest first.

SuggestedSearch.description: A search enrichment would start: a distinctive or unique value of a likely record, not yet searched for the person. A person starts it with POST .../searches, naming the record and the field.

SuggestedSearchKind.description: The kind of the value: one of the kinds the environment's enrichment setting names.

Usage.description: Body of the 200 answer to GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/usage: what the workspace's environments were metered for on each UTC day from from through to. Each billable unit is counted once, where it becomes final: an assessment when it is admitted (by flow and depth), a webhook delivery once per event per endpoint (retries and replays add nothing), a key-usage event once when the ingest accepts it, and a screened person once per screening when its result is recorded. A count does not change when the assessment, account or workspace is later deleted. A day, environment or metric with nothing counted has no item. No prices or billing; screening spend is in each screening's spent. console_lookups is the one limit: the live environment's daily cap on console lookups, as spent today.

workspace_id.description: The workspace id, which is also its live environment's workspace id; the test environment's is the same id with :test appended. A workspace created through the API is tnt_ and a 26-character ULID.

to.description: The last UTC day covered, included.

items.description: Ordered by environment (live first), then day, metric, flow and depth.

console_lookups.description: Present when the caller may read the live environment (a member allowed live, or a live key with the usage scope) and the API enforces the console lookup cap. Absent otherwise; it does not depend on from and to.

metric.description: assessments: assessments admitted. webhook_deliveries: events sent to endpoints, one per event per endpoint. key_usage_events: key-usage events accepted. screenings: people a screening recorded a final result for, one per person per screening; a failed person counts only when its lookups were kept.

external_user_id.description: The user's id at the identity provider the console signs people in with: 1 to 256 printable ASCII characters with no space, compared exactly.

console_credential_id.description: The public id of the console credential the user acted through.

principal_id.description: Stable workspace principal id, retained across identity-provider subject migration. Absent for older events.

Verdict.description: A reviewer's overrule (POST .../people/{person_id}/records), which decides joined whatever the likelihood and sticks for as long as a lookup finds the same record. Absent when nobody overruled it.

WebhookAggregateRequest.description: Count every retained matching attempt in [from,to). Capture is best effort; missing attempts cannot be inferred. UTC buckets may be partial at the edges. The window is at most 30 days.

endpoint_id.description: Opaque id of the endpoint registration.

event_id.description: The event id the receiver saw as NR-Webhook-Id and as the body's id. Replay it with POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/deliveries/{event_id}/replay.

event_type.description: The event's type, as its body's type: endpoint.verification, workspace.deleted, webhook_endpoint.disabled, audit.event, investigation.completed, or a type added later.

attempt.description: Which attempt of this delivery this was: 1 for the first send, up to 9 with retries. A replay counts its own attempts from 1.

replay.description: true for an attempt of a replay you asked for.

status.description: delivered when the endpoint answered 2xx; failed otherwise, with failure naming why.

response_code.description: The HTTP status the endpoint answered. Absent when no response was read.

failure.description: Why the attempt failed: the URL is no longer valid, the host did not resolve, it resolved to an address that is not public, no answer within 5 seconds, the connection failed, a 3xx (redirects are not followed) or another non-2xx status. Absent for a delivered attempt.

latency_ms.description: Milliseconds from sending the request to the answer or the failure.

attempted_at.description: When the request was sent. Its NR-Webhook-Timestamp is this time in Unix seconds.

WebhookDeliveryAttemptStatus.description: delivered when the endpoint answered 2xx; failed otherwise, with failure naming why.

WebhookDeliveryList.description: The 200 answer of GET /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/deliveries: one page of the endpoint's delivery attempts, newest first. Each item is one POST to the endpoint. Attempts are kept for 30 days, or the workspace's retention_days when that is shorter. next_cursor is present only when another page exists.

endpoint_id.description: Opaque id of the endpoint registration.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, MAC'd by the server and bound to the workspace and endpoint it was issued for. Pass it back unchanged as cursor; a tampered, foreign or expired cursor answers 400 invalid_cursor.

WebhookEndpoint.description: One of the workspace's registered webhook endpoints. Signing secrets are not part of it: a secret is shown once, when it is issued (POST /v1/webhooks and POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/rotate).

endpoint_id.description: Opaque id of the endpoint registration.

state.description: unverified until the endpoint echoes an endpoint.verification challenge (send one with POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/test); verified receives events; disabled after 72 hours of continuous delivery failure, and verified again by the same challenge.

response_mode.description: The response mode recorded for the endpoint. No event the API sends today differs by mode.

verified_at.description: When the endpoint last echoed a challenge. Absent until it first does.

failing_since.description: The first failed delivery attempt of the endpoint's current failure streak. Absent while its latest attempt succeeded, before any attempt failed, and after it is verified again.

last_failure_at.description: The latest failed delivery attempt of the current failure streak; present exactly when failing_since is. A failure more than 2 hours after it starts a new streak.

disabled_at.description: When the endpoint was disabled after failing continuously for 72 hours, as in the webhook_endpoint.disabled event. Present while state is disabled; absent before and after it is verified again.

signing_keys.description: The keys a receiver may see in NR-Webhook-Key-Id, oldest first. The last one signs every new delivery; an older one keeps verifying until its expires_at.

WebhookEndpointCreated.description: The 201 answer of POST /v1/webhooks: the new endpoint, unverified, and its first signing secret, shown once. Store the secret where the receiver reads it, then send endpoint.verification with POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/test.

WebhookEndpointDisabled.description: One of the environment's endpoints stopped receiving events: every delivery attempt to it failed from failing_since until disabled_at, 72 hours or more. Its queued deliveries are dropped. Fix the receiver and verify it again with POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/test (type endpoint.verification) to resume delivery.

failing_since.description: The first failed attempt of the unbroken failure streak.

disabled_at.description: When the endpoint was disabled; equal to the event's created_at.

id.description: The event id, equal to the NR-Webhook-Id header and across redeliveries and every endpoint the event fans out to.

created_at.description: When the event was created. Equal across redeliveries; the signing timestamp header is per delivery.

test.description: Present, and true, only on an event sent by POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/test: its data is a fixed example investigation, not one of the workspace's, so a receiver acknowledges it and applies nothing. Real events have no test member.

WebhookEndpointList.description: GET /v1/webhooks answer: every endpoint of the calling workspace, in every state, ordered by endpoint_id. A workspace holds at most 5, so there is no page.

WebhookEndpointRequest.description: POST /v1/webhooks body. The workspace is the API key that signs the request, so it is not a body member. The URL must be https on port 443 or 8443 with a DNS name, not an IP literal, and every address the name resolves to must be public.

url.description: Where deliveries are sent: an https URL on port 443 or 8443, with a DNS host and no userinfo or fragment, at most 2048 characters.

response_mode.description: The response mode recorded for the endpoint: standard (the default) or detailed, which needs an API key with the detailed scope as well. No event the API sends today differs by mode.

Deliveries are at least once and unordered: deduplicate on id, and keep an assessment only when its detail.assessment_version is newer than the one you hold. GET /v1/assessments/{assessment_id} stays authoritative.

previous_key_id.description: The key that signed until this rotation.

previous_key_expires_at.description: When the previous key stops verifying: 7 days after the rotation.
